method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Chip Selloff Hits Stocks as Oil Gains Lift Yields: Markets Wrap
Equities.reason: Broad market wrap linking rising oil and higher yields from Middle East escalation to a chip-led equity selloff — signals a risk-off impulse for equities driven by macro (yields/oil) rather than idiosyncratic stock news.

Equities.summary: Oil jumps as US-Iran hostilities escalate and investors go into ‘risk-off’ mode
Equities.reason: Confirms the dominant market narrative: geopolitical escalation -> oil up -> risk-off -> memory chipmakers/tech weakness. High relevance because it ties sector pain to macro risk sentiment and index moves.

Equities.title: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, reports 68% surge in June revenue
Equities.summary: Ahead of its second-quarter earnings, TSMC reported its June and first-half revenue for 2026.
Equities.reason: Positive datapoint for AI-driven demand and semiconductor fundamentals (TSMC revenue surge). Acts as a counterbalance to risk-off flows but is single-company/sector-specific so lower relevance vs macro headlines.

Equities.title: Chip stocks hit rocky patch. What's next?
Equities.reason: Analytical piece on the chip sector's renewed volatility — reinforces the prevailing narrative that chip leadership is under pressure amid macro/geopolitical and yield-driven headwinds.

Equities.title: Investors alarmed as Asian chipmakers take stranglehold on indices
Equities.summary: TSMC, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics together account for 29% of MSCI Emerging Markets index
Equities.reason: Highlights concentration risk of a few mega chip names in indices — increases systemic vulnerability to sector-specific shocks and amplifies market downside when chips wobble.

Rates.title: Treasury Two-Year Yields Rise to Highest Since 2025 as Oil Jumps
Rates.reason: Front-end US yields moving to multi-year highs (title) signals a bond selloff and repricing of near-term policy expectations; oil-driven risk and inflation concerns amplify rate-sensitivity — negative for bond prices and rates sentiment.

Rates.title: Shares skid, bond yields rise as Gulf conflict sends oil surging
Rates.reason: Headline links geopolitical risk and a sharp oil move to rising bond yields — a typical risk-off/geopolitical channel that pressures bonds (yields up), giving a negative impulse to rates.

Rates.title: Traders Grapple With World That’s Good for Dollar, Bad for Bonds
Rates.reason: Explicit market narrative: environment supportive of USD strength and hostile to bonds. That macro regime (dollar up, yields up) is a broad negative for fixed income and central to rates positioning.

Rates.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, June 16-17, 2026
Rates.summary: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, June 16-17, 2026
Rates.reason: FOMC minutes are a primary input on the policy path. In the current environment, minutes that are read as leaving tightening risks or delaying cuts act as a material negative for bond prices (higher-for-longer regime).

Rates.title: Banks’ Record Bond Short Sparks Quest for Answers
Rates.reason: Evidence of outsized bond short positions increases market vulnerability to further selling and liquidity stress — a structural negative for bond markets and rates volatility.

Rates.title: The Quarter-Trillion-Dollar Onslaught of AI Bonds Is Testing Investors’ Limits
Rates.reason: Large corporate bond issuance tied to AI investment represents supply pressure in credit and broader bond markets; incremental issuance is a modest negative for yields/prices when investors’ capacity is tested.

Rates.title: Japan pension pivot seen as a slow burn, not a bond market fire sale
Rates.reason: Headline suggests the pension-related shift in Japan is unlikely to trigger abrupt JGB supply shocks; that calms a specific source of bond-market stress and is marginally supportive for rates (positive for bond prices).

Rates.title: Meeting of 10-11 June 2026
Rates.reason: ECB meeting account provides guidance on euro-area policy path; in the current global tightening and yields-tilting-up backdrop, such minutes are more likely to reinforce rate-normalisation expectations — a mild negative for euro-area bond prices.

Commodities.reason: Higher US production is structurally bearish for global oil prices; directly offsets some of the geopolitical-driven risk premium — medium-high relevance.

Commodities.reason: Record US exports indicate tightening available supply in some regions and direct transmission of Hormuz disruption into demand for US barrels — constructive for prices but regionally focused.
